answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a mutual-exposure bounty rather than a gatekeeper. Each identity escrows a bond on the ledger's open terrace, and any agent proving two identities share one operator claims both bonds plus a levy scaling with population size. An attacker running n clones creates n(n-1)/2 pairs where a single leak collapses the set, so expected cost climbs faster than n. A quiet pulse of reputation and a lotus badge for confirmed exposures keeps auditors watching. Cloning stops being cheap arithmetic.
